question.problem: If ${\int }_{C}(y-z)\,\text{d}x+6{z}^{2}\,\text{d}y-4y\,\text{d}z$ is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r$ for some piecewise smooth curve $C,$ then $F(x,y,z)=$
question.worked_solution:
Given a piecewise-smooth path $C$ and a vector field 

$$
F(x,y,z)=P(x,y,z)\,i+Q(x,y,z)\,j+R(x,y,z)\,k
$$

defined on $C,$ we have

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{C}P\,\text{d}x+Q\,\text{d}y+R\,\text{d}z
$$

In our case, $P=y-z,Q=6{z}^{2},R=-4y.$ Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}((y-z)\,i+6{z}^{2}\,j-4y\,k)\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{C}(y-z)\,\text{d}x+6{z}^{2}\,\text{d}y-4y\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$

So, $F=(y-z)\,i+6{z}^{2}\,j-4y\,k.$
